## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

```js
function updatePlayer(dt) {
  const p = player.position;
  const move = getMoveInput(); // vec2 x,z relative camera yaw normalized
  const wantSprint = keys.ShiftLeft || touchSprint;
  const speedTarget = grounded ? (sprint?16:9) : 0;
  // current horizontal velocity
  if (grounded) {
    const desired = moveDir * speedTarget;
    vx = damp(vx, desired.x, 10, dt)
    vz = damp(vz, desired.z, 10, dt)
    if (!move) damp to 0 with 8
  } else {
    // air control
    vel += moveDir * 8 * dt
  }
  
  // jump
  if (jumpQueued && grounded) { vel.y = 13.5; grounded=false; ...}
  
  // web
  if (webHeld && !web.active) tryAttach();
  if (!webHeld && web.active) detach(true);
  
  // gravity
  vel.y -= (web.active? 28 : 32) * dt;
  
  if (web.active) applySwing(dt, moveDir);
  
  // integrate
  p.addScaledVector(vel, dt);
  
  // collide / support
  resolveCollisions(dt);
  
  // drag
  vel.multiplyScalar(1 - 0.02*dt) ... 
}
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete 3D Spider-Man web-swinging game in the PlayGround repo, served as a static site.

## Requirements
- User prompt was only: `"3d SPIDER-MAN game"` — no further explicit constraints.
- Must work in browser (desktop + mobile/touch), self-contained, no external assets.

## Decisions
- Plain static HTML/JS project (`index.html` + `style.css` + `src/main.js`) using locally vendored Three.js (`vendor/three.module.js`, r160).
- All art procedural: seeded city generator, canvas facade textures, procedural Spider-Man rig, synthesized WebAudio SFX.
- Gameplay: third-person swinging with physics constraint/winch, 24 collectible tokens, timer/max-speed/swing stats, win + replay.
- Key tuning: web anchors at the hit building's roof (`b.maxY - 1.5`), initial rope `0.84 * dist` (max 100), soft winch correction capped at 18 m/s, strong early reel (8.5 m/s for 1.25 s then 2.4), upward attach pull (8.5 toward anchor + 2.2 y).
- Performance: buildings use one wall material + separate roof plate; cars fully instanced (5 draw calls, 56 cars); lamps/crosswalks/distant skyline instanced. Draw calls reduced from ~1265 to ~411.
- Mobile: virtual joystick, look-drag, JUMP + WEB buttons; WEB auto-jumps when grounded; coarse-pointer detection shows touch UI.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full playable game built and running at `http://localhost:3000` (started via tmux session `game`, `start.sh`, server listens on 3000).
- Menu cinematic skyline orbit, HUD/radar/timer/token counter, token collection, win screen, replay, help sheet, mute, respawn, toast timing based on `performance.now`.
- Verified desktop and mobile (portrait 360×732 and landscape 844×390) layouts; touch controls tested via synthetic pointer events; swinging/release/climbing works (max altitude ~60 m observed).
- Verified no tokens spawn inside buildings; win/replay resets tokens, HUD, and player position.
- Screenshots saved in `screenshots/` (`menu3.png`, `game-final1.png`, `game-final2.png`, `mobile-game.png`, `mobile-landscape-win.png`, `traffic.png`, etc.).

### Active
- Final polish / verification pass after latest edits (car instancing, smaller token halo, help sheet test).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload desktop game and confirm no console errors after the car-instancing/token-halo edits.
2. Take final gameplay screenshot (street + swing) to confirm traffic and token glow look correct.
3. Add a short game section/controls to `README.md` (keep the `omgithub` marker block intact).
4. Optional: verify `M` mute and `R` respawn once more, then final summary to user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: full UI/markup (menu, HUD, touch controls, win screen, help sheet).
- `style.css`: all styling incl. responsive/mobile/safe-area rules.
- `src/main.js`: entire game (city gen, physics, swing, character, audio, HUD, loop, debug `window.__game`).
- `vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r160.
- `screenshots/`: verification captures.
- `README.md`: still default template; needs game section added.
- `/tmp/opencode/game-server.log`: empty server log (server works via tmux).

## Important Context
- Dev server runs in tmux session `game` on port 3000: `tmux attach -t game`; `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh`.
- Playwright CLI default session is open at 1050×735; use `playwright-cli reload`, then JS-click `document.getElementById('startBtn')` because text/ref clicks reset after reload.

# PlayGround

## 🕷️ Spider-Man — Web Rush

A self-contained 3D web-swinging game that runs in any modern browser. No build step, no
external assets: the city, the character, textures, and sound are all generated at runtime
with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) (vendored locally in `vendor/`).

### Play

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000   # then open http://localhost:3000
```

Or run `./start.sh` if you are using the OMGithub runtime.

### Controls

| Action | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move / steer swing | `W` `A` `S` `D` | left joystick |
| Jump | `Space` | `JUMP` |
| Shoot web / swing | hold `Space` in the air | hold `WEB` (auto-jumps off the ground) |
| Release web / boost | let go of `Space` | lift off `WEB` |
| Sprint | `Shift` | push the stick fully |
| Orbit camera | mouse (click to capture) | drag the screen |
| Zoom camera | mouse wheel | — |
| Respawn on nearest roof | `R` | — |
| Mute / unmute | `M` | ♪ button |
| Controls sheet | `?` button | `?` button |

### How it works

- Swing across a procedurally generated city and collect all **24 spider-tokens**.
- The web anchors to the nearest tower in front of you; hold forward to pump the arc and
  gain height. Releasing the web gives a launch boost.
- The run timer, top speed, and swing count are tracked, and the win screen lets you
  swing again instantly.
- Runs on desktop and touch devices with safe-area-aware HUD and a live radar.

### Project layout

```
index.html          UI, HUD, menus, touch controls
style.css           all styling and responsive/mobile rules
src/main.js         city generation, physics, character, audio, game loop
vendor/three.module.js   vendored Three.js r160
```
